messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated gateway 5xx + timeouts for tenant MeridianForge on ap-southeast-2-dedicated-7. Rule: gateway_error_rate > 5% (3m). Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-gateway-errors

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty INC-91234 created and routed to oncall (nora). Severity: P1.

nora: taking pager. starting triage. tagging infra + runtime. cc @cs-ops for customer comms.

ben: what error split are we seeing? 502 vs 504 vs upstream resets?

yoshi: quick sample from gproxy and worker logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:03:12Z] req=7a9e gateway: upstream_status=504 tenant=MeridianForge route=/v1/chat upstream_timeout=true
[2026-03-15T14:03:13Z] req=7aa0 worker: kv_evict tenant=MeridianForge pool=dedicated-7 evictions=213
[2026-03-15T14:03:14Z] req=7ab1 worker: upstream_err=connection_reset tenant=MeridianForge target=worker-4
```

tasha: infra dashboards: pool ap-southeast-2-dedicated-7 node count=5; overall GPU util ~72% but NVMe I/O saturation ~98% on nodes 3 & 4. p95 latency for tenant requests jumped 150ms -> 1.4s. global KV eviction rate spiked. Looks like IO-bound thrash.

ben: any heavy tenants on that pool right now?

yoshi: hitting audit: OmnidataCorp launched a large bulk-ranked-embeddings batch at 13:58Z targeting same pool (burst of batched requests, large contexts). Their concurrency jumped to 120. That correlates.

nora: immediate mitigations (short window): 1) place MeridianForge on protected fallback routing to reduce user-visible errors 2) throttle OmnidataCorp concurrency to 20 3) enable per-tenant KV soft limits on pool 4) request +2 worker nodes from autoscaler. I'll run commands.

yoshi: applying throttle for OmnidataCorp now:
```bash
redwoodctl tenant throttle set --tenant OmnidataCorp --pool ap-southeast-2-dedicated-7 --max-concurrency 20 --reason "noisy batch causing KV IO thrash"
```

infra-bot: throttle applied. OmnidataCorp concurrency capped at 20.

tasha: autoscaler: requested +2 workers for ap-southeast-2-dedicated-7, ETA ~4m.

yoshi: enable KV soft eviction thresholds for MeridianForge and pool-level holdoff:
```yaml
# applied via orchestration
kv:
  tenant: MeridianForge
  soft_eviction_pct: 7
  hold_off_seconds: 90
```

ben: routing MeridianForge to fallback-pool (canary 100%) to stop ongoing failures.

nora: command: 
```bash
redwoodctl routing set-tenant-route --tenant MeridianForge --target fallback-ap-southeast --note "mitigate 5xx due to NVMe thrash"
```

cs-ops: I've messaged MeridianForge support: "We see elevated errors and have routed your traffic to a protected pool and limited the noisy tenant. Expect reduced errors within ~10 minutes while we scale and stabilize. We'll follow up with a postmortem." They asked for real-time updates.

infra-bot: Autoscaler: provisioning 2 nodes for ap-southeast-2-dedicated-7; joined pool in 3m 50s.

ben: after throttle + routing + KV changes: short snapshot -> gateway_5xx_rate dropped from 8.6% -> 2.9% for MeridianForge traffic. NVMe utilization on nodes 3/4 dropped to ~60%. p95 latency ~250ms.

yoshi: remain monitoring connection_reset patterns. so far resets decreased significantly.

nora: rolling-remediate: draining suspect node worker-4 (high IO wait) for kernel-level clean, cordon then restart. command: 
```bash
redwoodctl node drain worker-4 --pool ap-southeast-2-dedicated-7 --reason "clear sockets/io backlog"
```

infra-bot: worker-4 drained and restarted; health checks OK.

ben: reintroducing MeridianForge to primary pool gradually: 10% -> 30% -> 60% over 15m with health-check gating.

yoshi: metrics after first 30m: MeridianForge 5xx -> 0.8%, p95 180-220ms, KV eviction back to baseline. OmnidataCorp throttle holding; their batches queued up but progressing.

cs-ops: MeridianForge acknowledged update & requested a short RCA with timeline. They asked if we can avoid cross-tenant IO interference longer term.

nora: next steps/followups: - open INC-91234 ticket with timeline and logs - schedule postmortem with runtime + infra + product (MeridianForge impacted) - consider pool-level tenant QoS defaults (concurrency, I/O cgroups), and autoscaler sensitivity to nvme iops - advise CS on standard customer comms template for noisy neighbor incidents

ben: handoff: I'll stay for 25m to watch canary. Yoshi, can you own the RCA writeup? tag runtime+infra.

yoshi: taking RCA. I'll collect kernel metrics, nvme iostat traces, and OmnidataCorp request profile.

nora: resolving pager for now; marking incident P1 -> mitigated. Leaving channel. (reacted :white_check_mark: by cs-ops)

infra-bot: Incident state updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Reminder to file postmortem within 72h.

ben: noted. closing temporary throttles on OmnidataCorp once postmortem action item decides. For now keeping them capped for 2h.

yoshi: created postmortem stub INC-91234-PM and attached initial graphs. Will ping owners.

cs-ops: customer satisfied with immediate mitigation, requested SLA review. Logged request to INC-91234.

ben: handing off oncall to tasha in 20m. if anything spikes escalate to pager. Great work team. :clap:

tasha: oncall ack, will monitor.
